notes: The privacy and Google-data pages now render according to the deployment's actual privacy behaviour instead of assuming the default. Both /privacy and /google-data become server-rendered on demand (export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic', an established pattern in this repo) and read GROWTH_PRIVACY_FILTER at request time; bootstrap/compose.yml now passes that key to the web service as well (previously only api/worker/dispatcher had it). Both pages state the default behaviour — the platform removes detail rows that look like email addresses, phone numbers or long digit runs, token/secret assignments, control characters or over-long text; removed rows never reach reports, exports or analysis input, and the day is recorded as incomplete — and, only when the deployment runs with GROWTH_PRIVACY_FILTER=off, additionally disclose that this deployment keeps the raw rows: Google query terms are stored, displayed and exported exactly as returned, may contain personal data a visitor typed into a search box, and are also sent as analysis input to the AI provider the organization itself configured. /terms and /about stay statically prerendered and are unaffected. Local verification: the web production build passes; the build manifest shows /privacy and /google-data as dynamic/server while /terms and /about remain static; a local production instance renders the disclosure with the switch off and omits it (while still showing the default statement) in the default strict mode. No SQL migration and no schema change. Rollback to v0.2.19 is compatible; because the page reads the switch per request, rolling an application back while leaving GROWTH_PRIVACY_FILTER=off would restore the older page text, which no longer discloses that filtering is off.
